title: Automated Legacy Code Migration for Financial Systems
business: Large-scale financial institutions maintaining massive, aging COBOL and Java codebases.
problem: Manual refactoring of legacy code is prohibitively expensive and prone to human error, leading to significant technical debt and integration delays.
solution: Utilizing GPT-5.4 Mini to act as an intelligent subagent that performs automated code analysis, generates unit tests, and applies patches to legacy modules, leveraging its specialized computer use and code interpreter capabilities.
steps: Ingest legacy source files into the model context using the 400,000 token window.
Deploy subagents to perform static analysis and identify refactoring candidates.
Use the apply_patch tool to programmatically suggest and implement code improvements.
Validate changes by running generated unit tests within the hosted shell environment.
Commit verified patches to the version control system.
outcome: A streamlined, repeatable pipeline for modernizing legacy systems that reduces manual intervention and accelerates deployment cycles.
limitation: The model may occasionally hallucinate logic in highly complex, non-standard legacy syntax; verify output by checking the consistency of the applied patches against the original business logic requirements.
